paper_title: On the Transformation Capability of Feasible Mechanisms for Programmable Matter
statement: There are also some promising specific technical questions: What is the exact complexity of RotC-Transformability? What is the complexity of computing the optimum transformation? Can it be satisfactorily approximated? Finally, regarding the distributed transformations, there are various interesting variations of the model considered here, that would make sense. One of them is to assume nodes that are oblivious w.r.t. their orientation.
context: We intentionally restricted attention to very minimal actuation mechanisms. More sophisticated mechanical operations would enable a larger set of transformations and possibly also reduce the time complexity. Such an example is the ability of a node to become inserted between two neighboring nodes. There are also some promising specific technical questions: What is the exact complexity of RotC-Transformability? What is the complexity of computing the optimum transformation? Can it be satisfactorily approximated? Finally, regarding the distributed transformations, there are various interesting variations of the model considered here, that would make sense. One of them is to assume nodes that are oblivious w.r.t. their orientation.
